findings.title: remove() now unconditionally hits the underlying JPA store even when the IDP is already cached
findings.body: In remove(), `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is now executed unconditionally before the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` check. Previously, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only called inside the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch; when the cache entry was valid, the code used the already-cached `CachedIdentityProvider` (`cached.getIdentityProvider()`) without touching the delegate at all. After this change, every call to remove() performs an extra round-trip to the underlying storage (JPA/DB) even in the common case where the alias is already present in cache, which is pure overhead introduced only to support the new `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` call. The same information could be derived from `cached.getIdentityProvider()` in the else-branch instead of re-fetching from the delegate, avoiding the redundant query.

findings.title: Test cleanup references the literal alias "alias" instead of the actual created IDP alias, leaking test data
findings.body: In the new testCacheIDPForLogin test, cleanup is registered with `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (also repeated at line 425 for the "idp-alias-20" provider). The literal string "alias" is passed instead of the actual alias used when creating the provider (e.g. "idp-alias-" + i). This means the cleanup never removes the 20+ identity providers created by the test; at best the cleanup call fails (no IDP with alias "alias" exists), and the created identity providers remain in the realm after the test finishes. This leftover state can pollute subsequent tests in the same realm (e.g. IDP count assertions, alias uniqueness on re-run, or other cache tests), causing flaky or order-dependent test failures.

findings.title: No test coverage for invalidating warm login caches via create()/remove() of a currently login-eligible IDP
findings.body: testCacheIDPForLogin only exercises the create()/remove() invalidation paths (registerIDPLoginInvalidation) with IDPs that do NOT qualify for login (e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-1").remove()` removes a disabled, non-login IDP, and the newly created idp-alias-20 is initially hideOnLogin=true). The 20 initial IDP creations happen before any cache is warmed, so they never actually exercise invalidation of a populated cache either. As a result, the scenario where a currently login-eligible IDP is created or removed after the login caches are already populated (which should trigger registerIDPLoginInvalidation to clear all FetchMode caches) is never verified; only the analogous update() path (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) is thoroughly tested. A regression in the create()/remove() invalidation logic for this case would not be caught by this test.
